Under the terms of the agreement, Paramount

must release 30 films per year in the first two years, including 20 wide releases, and 32 films per year in years three, four, and five. At least four independent films must be released annually. Missing these targets will trigger a $30M penalty per film paid into union health and retirement funds.

commits to spend an additional $1.5B on U.S. film production over five years and is required to remain in California and maintain physical production lots for both Paramount and Warner Bros. in California.
The studio must also contribute $5M annually to an independent film purchasing fund and $47.5M over five years to a workforce training and development fund for displaced employees.
Paramount also agreed to establish an independent editorial board for CNN and CBS comprised only of journalists with no political bias.
For its cable network assets, the company must negotiate basic cable channel distribution for its networks completely independent from Warner Bros. Discovery channels to maintain competitive pricing.
The terms were discussed by California Attorney General Rob Bonta at a press conference on Monday.

“I’d rather resolve the case in the boardroom rather than the courtroom, and that’s what happened here,” Bonta said.
The deal is expected to close before October 1.
